target_customer: Apparel brands and retailers wanting fewer returns and higher conversion, and their online shoppers
problem: Shoppers cannot tell how clothes will fit and look online, causing returns and abandoned carts.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to apparel brands
product_category: Virtual try-on and 3D avatar fit technology

founders.name: David Pastewka
education: UC Berkeley, Business and Computer Science

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a believable 3D avatar and garment fit from shopper inputs and brand data was computer vision and graphics heavy for a seven person team.

defensibility.rationale: Fit data from brands could compound, but rivals such as Zeekit and Metail already existed and big retailers could acquire or build.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Gap acquired Drapr in August 2021; Walmart separately acquired Zeekit.

market_need_then: Online apparel returns were a known cost and the pandemic in 2020 accelerated online shopping; Gap framed the deal as reducing unnecessary returns. No dated spend figures were found.

branding.domain_note: drapr.com, exact .com, history not found; the domain did not resolve when fetched.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand coverage found beyond acquisition news; a B2B tool with no public brand.

outcome_analysis: Drapr's founders had built and sold a 3D scanning company earlier and returned to virtual try-on. Within about a year of the YC batch, Gap acquired the team and technology in August 2021 to improve fit and cut returns, a quick strategic exit likely close to an acqui-hire given the small team and tiny disclosed funding.
notes: Funding is unverified: only CB Insights shows 630K over 4 rounds including a seed on 2020-08-25, with garbled amounts, so no round is recorded.
